Output_CacheWriteTokensDetails.description: Non-overlapping write counts by lifetime; their sum is `cache_write_tokens`.

Output_CaptureDetailDto.description: One physical capture, readable even when the downstream log is disabled.

Output_CaptureEventDto.description: One stream chunk or websocket message.

direction.description: `request` (client to gateway, gateway to provider) or `response`.

sequence.description: Monotonic across both directions of the exchange or connection.

Output_CaptureRecordDto.description: One captured exchange in full, downstream or upstream.

initiatorRequestId.description: Initiating request for provenance; actual associations are many-to-many.

metrics.description:
Upstream-native usage for this one exchange, when the channel reported
any. Billed usage is on the usage record, not here.

Output_ChannelCapabilities.description:
Optional abilities beyond protocol operations. All false is a legitimate
channel: an API-key upstream needs none of them.

paidUsage.description:
`QuotaModel::allows_paid_usage` reads the credential metadata flag
`allow_paid_usage`, so the console offers the switch. Not derivable
either: the method has a default, and overriding it is invisible here.

quotaQuery.description: `QuotaQuery`: the upstream can be asked about the account's balance.

quotaReset.description: `QuotaReset`: a spent window can be reopened against the upstream.

refresh.description: `CredentialRefresh`: the credential can be renewed without a person.

services.description: `ChannelServices`: non-protocol endpoints of the upstream's own client.

websocket.description:
The channel serves at least one operation over a WebSocket. Not
derivable from an accessor; a channel that overrides a socket operation
declares it.

Output_ChannelDescriptor.description: A channel as the management layer sees it.

credentialKinds.description: Stored credential types accepted on manual creation, distinct from login flows.

loginModes.description: Empty means no login flow is offered for this channel.

Output_ConfigKey.description:
One entry of a provider's configuration. Unless noted, the name is a key of
the provider's `config` JSON; `base_url` is the provider's own column.

placeholder.description: Display-only default or URL template; never written into config by the UI.

required.description:
The provider cannot serve a request without it. Everything else has a
channel default.

Output_ConfigKeyKind.description: How a configuration value is written, for form rendering and validation.

oneOf.description: Any other JSON shape: an array, or an object that is not headers.
HTTP header names, or header name/value pairs.

Output_ConfigurationDataDto.description:
Every exported table, in the order a fresh instance may replay them: a row
never appears before the row it points at. Each field defaults to empty, so
a document written by a build that knew fewer tables still imports.

settings.description:
The single settings row. `config_revision` travels but is never
imported: the destination's revision is its own counter.

Output_ConfigurationExportDto.description: One instance's configuration as a document.

secrets.description:
The sealing codecs the exported blobs actually use, sorted and without
duplicates; empty when the secrets were omitted. An importer reads it
before it starts, to decide whether it needs a source master key at all.

secretsOmitted.description:
True when the export was taken without secrets: every credential's
`secret` is null.

Output_ConnectionProfileDto.description: A reusable HTTP transport configuration, independent of outbound proxy selection.

emulation.description: A `gproxy-client` emulation object, or null. wreq applies the full identity; other clients apply supported custom fields.

Output_ConnectivityResultDto.description:
What the edge looks like from here. `ip` and `colo` come from Cloudflare's
trace endpoint, so `ip` is the address the upstream would see — which is
the whole point of testing a proxy.

colo.description: The Cloudflare edge that answered, e.g. `NRT`.

latencyMs.description:
Measured across the whole exchange, including the body read, and
reported for a failure too.

context_management.description: Required key; the reference allows null.

Output_CredentialCreated.description:
A login that produced a credential row. The secret is already sealed in the
database; nothing about it travels back.

Output_CredentialCycleDto.description:
One period of one upstream window on a credential, with the USD this
deployment settled against it.

closedAtMs.description: None while the cycle is open.

costUsd.description:
USD settled against the cycle through this deployment. Final once
closed.

endsAtMs.description: None for a window that never ends.

estimatedAllowanceUsd.description:
`sample.costUsd / sample.usedPercent * 100`: the USD the whole window
would hold at the rate this cycle has been spending, when the sample
reports a positive percent. It only sees traffic through this
deployment, so use elsewhere on the same account reads it low.

sample.description:
The latest upstream reading on the cycle; for a closed cycle, the
last one before it closed.

windowId.description:
The observed `QuotaEntry.id`, the declared dimension id before any
observation, or `month` for a credential that declares no window.

Output_CredentialDto.description:
A credential without its secret. Only presence and expiry timestamps are
exposed; reading the material itself requires `Credentials::reveal_secret`.

organizationId.description: Opaque to this crate: the application layer decides what owns what.

refreshExpiresAtMs.description:
Read-only refresh-token expiry, projected from the sealed secret on management reads.
None means no expiry was reported or the secret could not be read.

version.description: Bumped by every secret or lifecycle write; peers reload on a change.

Output_CredentialLimitStatusDto.description: An operator limit's current window on one credential.

Output_CredentialQuotaDto.description:
What this instance knows about one credential's upstream quota: its
cycles — every open one and each window's most recent closed ones — and
the blocks currently keeping it out of selection.

Windows overlap (a 5-hour and a weekly window both count the same
request), so the cycles' costs are never meant to be summed across
windows. The raw readings behind the cycles are a separate, paged read.

blocks.description: Only blocks that have not expired yet.

cycles.description:
Open cycles first, by window; then closed ones by window, newest
first.

Output_CredentialSummaryDto.description: What a refresh reports back: never secret material, only its identity.

Output_CycleSampleDto.description: One upstream reading, kept on a cycle as a set taken at `atMs`.

costUsd.description: The cycle's `costUsd` when the reading was taken.

Output_DefaultModelCatalogDto.description:
The bundled catalog, exactly as the asset spells it. Its numbers are
checked against its own rows at load: a truncated asset is a build problem
and should be found once, not per lookup.

Output_DefaultModelDto.description:
One catalog entry. `model_id` is the unqualified model name; the
unmodelled keys — modalities, supported parameters, reasoning levels — stay
in `metadata`, which is exactly the shape the `models.metadata` column
holds.

price.description: A decimal string: this is money and must not pass through a float.

unitSize.description: `1000000` for the token metrics, `1` for counted ones.

Output_DefaultModelPricingDto.description:
The price book for one model: a glob, its rates, and the context or
service-tier overrides above them.

modelPattern.description:
A `*fragment*` glob. The longer the fragment, the more specific the
rule, which is what `priority` encodes.

Output_DefaultModelTierDto.description:
A long-context or service-tier override. Every price is optional and every
absent one inherits the rule's rates.

reasoning.description: Alternative compatible-provider spelling. Kept separately on the wire.

reasoning_content.description: Plain-text reasoning returned by compatible providers (for example DeepSeek).

Output_DeviceCodeResponse.description: RFC 8628 §3.2. `device_code` is plaintext and exists only here.

device_code.description: The secret the device polls with.

user_code.description:
The short code the person types, in the grouped form they read off the
screen. Lookups normalize it, so any spelling with the right characters
resolves.

verification_uri_complete.description:
The same page with the code already filled in, for a device that can
show a QR code (RFC 8628 §3.3.1).

Output_DeviceDecided.description: The outcome of an approval-page decision or a cancellation.

Output_DeviceDetails.description: What the approval page renders for a pending device authorization.

expires_at_ms.description:
Milliseconds, unlike the RFC fields above: this one is for a page this
repository renders, not for the device.

Output_DevicePollOutcome.description:
One polling step. The SDK never sleeps and never loops: the caller owns the
cadence, and `interval_secs` is what it should honour.

oneOf.description: Nobody has approved it yet. Poll again after `interval_secs`.

The person refused. The session is gone; starting again is the only way
forward.
The user code outlived its window. The session is gone.

expiresAtMs.description: When the upstream stops accepting this user code, if it said.

intervalSecs.description:
How long to wait before the first poll, and between polls. The upstream
may raise it; a `Pending` answer always carries the current value.

userCode.description: What the person types on the other device.

verificationUriComplete.description:
The same page with the code already filled in, where the upstream
offers one.

Output_DiscoveredModelDto.description: One model an upstream says it offers.

hasDefaultPrice.description:
Whether the bundled catalog can price it without an operator writing a
rule by hand.

hasPrice.description: A saved provider or global rule matches this upstream model.

known.description: Whether this provider already has a `provider_models` row for it.

Output_ExportCredentialDto.description:
A credential row plus the sealed bytes behind it. The columns are flattened,
so the object is a [`CredentialDto`] with one field added.

organizationId.description: Opaque to this crate: the application layer decides what owns what.

refreshExpiresAtMs.description:
Read-only refresh-token expiry, projected from the sealed secret on management reads.
None means no expiry was reported or the secret could not be read.

secret.description: The database column verbatim; null when the export omitted secrets.

version.description: Bumped by every secret or lifecycle write; peers reload on a change.

Output_FileSize.description: ProtoJSON int64 values encode as strings; parsers also accept JSON integers.

oneOf.description: This hop ended, but generation requires another request with its token.

access_programs.description: Newer API responses report this even when null; older responses omit it.

error.description: A Google API error can arrive as a record inside a successful HTTP stream.

Output_HistoryDeleted.description: How many history rows a deletion removed.

Output_ImportReportDto.description:
What one import did. The counters are rows, across every kind; the warnings
are the things that were silently changed rather than refused, which is the
only place a caller learns that a credential arrived unusable.

skipped.description:
Rows the document named that were not written, which today is exactly
the credentials whose secret could not be opened. What `Replace`
deleted is reported as a warning instead: a removal is not a skip.

Output_InstanceSettingsDto.description:
Identity, network, execution limits and maintenance. `config_revision` is
read-only: it is the write path's own counter.

alwaysSecureCookie.description: Absent in an export from a build without it, which reads as off.

hasTokenizerAuthToken.description:
The vocabulary source token is sealed like a credential secret; only
its presence is reported.

quotaObservationRetentionDays.description:
Days of upstream quota observations to keep; None keeps them all.
Cycles are never pruned. Absent in an older export, which reads as
the 90-day default.

retentionDays.description: Days of completed request captures to keep; None keeps them all.

usageRetentionDays.description:
Days of usage records to keep; None keeps them all. Usage statistics
and totals are computed from these. Absent in an older export, which
reads as keeping everything.

Output_InteractionStepBody.description: Fields shared by native step variants; vendor-specific fields remain in rest.

Output_LiveInt64.description: ProtoJSON int64 fields allow decimal strings and numeric JSON inputs.

Output_LogBodyDto.description: One captured body, or the reason there is none.

bytes.description: Reconstructed body bytes, not the length of `content`.

state.description:
The record's own `body_state`: `not_captured`, `recording`,
`complete`, `partial` or `failed`. `not_captured` with zero bytes is a
body nobody stored; `complete` with zero bytes is a body that was
genuinely empty.

truncated.description: Compatibility field: false, because reads return the complete stored payload.

Output_LogBodyEncoding.description: How a body's bytes are spelled in `content`.

oneOf.description: Valid UTF-8.
Standard base64 with padding, for bytes that are not text.

Output_LogDetailDto.description: One request and everything captured under it.

events.description:
The events of the downstream record and of every upstream one,
ordered by capture and then by sequence.

eventsTruncated.description: True when the event cap cut the list short.

upstream.description:
Every associated upstream call, ordered by start time, attempt ordinal and ID.
A retry is another entry here, not another downstream record.

usage.description: Usage of associated physical upstream calls, retained independently of captures.

Output_LogEntryDto.description: One downstream request or physical upstream exchange, as a list row.

requestId.description:
Capture ID. For downstream rows this is also the request ID;

state.description:
`in_progress`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Capture

Output_LogPageDto.description: One page of the request list, plus where the next one starts.

nextCursor.description:

Hand both cursor halves back unchanged to get the next page.

Output_LoginMode.description: How a credential for this channel comes into existence.

oneOf.description: Browser redirect with PKCE; `OAuthAuthorizationCode`.

anyOf.description: Earlier Responses references represented MCP errors as strings.

created.description: Some compatible catalogs do not report a creation timestamp.

shutdown_date.description: Announced shutdown date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); explicit `null` when none is announced.

priceRules.description: Saved, enabled rules matching this model, in billing precedence order.

line.description: Provider-reported model line; new lines are allowed without inferring from IDs.

Output_ModelReasoningEffort.description:
Catalog effort choices include CLI modes such as Ultra and Persistent;

status.description: The upstream's HTTP status, or 0 when nothing was answered.

usage.description:
What the upstream reported it spent. Absent when it reported nothing,

deletedAtMs.description:
Set by `retire`, cleared when the same id is registered again. A

id.description: The public `client_id`, chosen at registration and immutable after it.

role.description:

instance role.

modelPattern.description:
A glob: `*` and `?`, anchored, case-sensitive. `*` matches a request
that names no model at all.

priority.description: Higher wins; ties fall back to id order.

userId.description:
Exactly one of these two is set. A rule with neither is a grant to
nobody; a rule with both is an intersection the snapshot still honours
but this family refuses to write, because nobody who wrote one meant
"the key *and* the user".

Output_PortalContextDto.description:
Everything a portal needs to render its shell, in one call: who you are,
which scopes you belong to, what you are subscribed to, and which parts of
the portal this instance offers you.

organizations.description:
Direct organization memberships. A team joined without its parent is
*not* listed here; the team is, with its `organizationId`.

Output_PortalFeaturesDto.description:
What this instance lets this caller do, so a portal can hide a tab rather
than render one that answers 403.

Every flag is a fact about configuration or about the caller's role — never
about data — so computing it costs nothing and leaks nothing.

canChangePassword.description:
Same rule, same reason: a third-party program does not get to change
the account password it was lent.

canCreateKeys.description:
Whether the key family's writing half is open. False for an OAuth-grant
caller: a token the user handed to somebody else's program must not be
able to mint a fresh long-lived credential out of that trust.

canSeeConsole.description:
Whether to offer a link into the operator console: it has to be built
into this instance *and* the caller has to be an instance administrator.

Output_PortalKeyCreated.description:
A minted or rotated key. `token` is the only time the plaintext travels,
apart from an explicit reveal of a key that retained one.

hasSecret.description:
Whether the instance retained a sealed copy, i.e. whether `reveal` can
answer for this key.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key body, for telling two keys apart.

Output_PortalKeyDto.description:
One of the caller's own gateway keys.

No `userId`: it is always the caller. No `kind`: the portal only ever shows
`user` keys, because an `oauth` key belongs to a grant and is managed by
revoking that grant.

hasSecret.description:
Whether the instance retained a sealed copy, i.e. whether `reveal` can
answer for this key.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key body, for telling two keys apart.

Output_PortalKeySecretDto.description:
The answer to a reveal. Separate from [`PortalKeyDto`] so a plaintext can
never ride along with an ordinary read.

Output_PortalModelDto.description:
One addressable model name, and whether this caller may call it.

`providerCount` and `channelIds` describe the providers that back the name
on this instance, not the ones this caller may reach — a count and a
channel id are instance configuration, and knowing that `codex/gpt-5` is
served by two providers tells a user nothing about another tenant.
`permitted` is the caller's own answer.

channelIds.description: The channels behind the name, sorted and deduplicated.

name.description: Either an exposed model name or a `providerName/model` form.

permitted.description:
Whether at least one of those providers is one the caller's permission
rules allow for this name.

Output_PortalOAuthSessionDto.description: One live authorization the caller granted to a third-party client.

clientName.description:
The client's registered display name, or None when the registration is
gone.

loggedInAtMs.description:
The first successful token exchange. None means consent was given but
the client never completed the login.

scopes.description: The scopes this grant carries, as granted.

Output_PortalQuotaWindowDto.description:
One budget window of the caller's own chain.

The owner is reported because a user has to be able to tell "I am out of my
own allowance" from "my team is out of its allowance", which are two very
different things to do something about. Every owner here is one the caller
is themselves part of: the chain is built from their own key binding.

modelPattern.description: The glob this budget covers, absent when it covers everything.

usedPercent.description:
On the 0..100 scale, to two decimals. None when the limit is zero,
which is a switched-off subject rather than a ratio.

windowKey.description: The budget's stable key within its owner, e.g. `primary`.

Output_PortalRequestDto.description:
One of the caller's own recent requests, reduced.

What is missing is the point: no bodies, no headers, no URL, no client
address, no credential id, and no provider id — only the provider's display
name, and only when it still exists. See the module note on
[`Portal::recent_requests`](crate::operations::Portal::recent_requests).

apiKeyId.description: The caller's own key that made the request, when one did.

durationMs.description: End minus start, when the request has ended.

model.description: The name the client asked for.

provider.description: The upstream's display name. Never its id, never its credential.

state.description:
`in_progress`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Capture
completeness, not the upstream's verdict.

role.description:
`member` or `admin`, scoped to this team. An organization admin is not
automatically a team admin.

Output_PortalUsageDto.description: The caller's own usage over the requested range.

hasPassword.description:
Whether a password is set. An account without one signs in through
OAuth only, and its password change takes no `current`.

role.description:
The instance-wide role, `admin` or `user`. Organization and team roles
are memberships and are listed with their scope.

Output_PriceRateDto.description:
One billable quantity's price. `value` buys `unit_quantity` units, so a
per-million token price is `unit_quantity = 1000000`.

conditions.description: None is the fallback rate; otherwise a nonempty object of dimensions.

metric.description: A `gproxy_store::entity::pricing::metric` key, or a custom one.

modelPattern.description: A `*`/`?` glob over the upstream model name.

operation.description: None covers every operation of the matched model.

providerId.description: None prices every provider; a provider rule wins over a global one.

Output_PriceTierDto.description:
A context or service-tier override inside one rule. Every per-million
price is optional: None inherits, zero is explicitly free.

serviceTier.description: None is a context tier; otherwise `standard`, `priority`, `flex`, … .

ttl.description:
Minimum lifetime of this breakpoint; omitted inherits the request TTL.
OpenAI OpenAPI: PromptCacheBreakpointParam (2026-10-21).

Output_PromptCacheBreakpointTtl.description:
Explicit cache-breakpoint lifetimes from OpenAI's PromptCacheBreakpointParam.
Separate from the request-wide PromptCacheTTLEnum and legacy retention policy.

Output_PromptCacheTtl.description:
Request-wide lifetimes from upstream_docs/openai/docs/Prompt caching.md.
The 2026-10-20 release predates the reference's request-level TTL enum update.

Output_PromptVariableValue.description: Prompt variables are a closed union, not arbitrary JSON (source line 4419).

channel.description:
The channel implementation this provider speaks through; must be one
of `Gproxy::channels()`.

config.description: Channel-specific configuration; always a JSON object.

requestTimeoutMs.description: Upstream response wait in milliseconds; None inherits the global setting.

streamIdleTimeoutMs.description: Maximum stream silence in milliseconds; None inherits the global setting.

hasPrice.description: A saved enabled provider or global price rule matches; populated by reads.

priceRules.description: Saved, enabled rules matching this model, in billing precedence order.

upstreamName.description: The name this provider's upstream answers to, not the public one.

Output_ProviderRuleSetDto.description: A rule set attached to a provider, in attachment order.

Output_QuotaAllowanceDto.description: None means the upstream did not report the field, never zero.

Output_QuotaDto.description:
One configured budget or operator limit. `owner_kind` is a free string:
`user`, `api_key`, `team`, `org` and `pool` are caller budgets the host
names per request, while `credential` and `provider` are operator limits on
upstream accounts. Both live in one table because both are windows over a
metric.

metric.description: `cost` for a budget; `requests` or `cost` for a limit.

modelPattern.description: A `*`/`?` glob over the upstream model name; absent covers everything.

windowKey.description: Stable key within the owner, e.g. `primary`.

Output_QuotaObservationDto.description:
One persisted upstream reading of one window: a row of the observation
log the cycles are built from.

cycleCostUsd.description:
That cycle's `costUsd` when the reading was taken; the difference
between two readings of one cycle is the USD spent between them.

cycleId.description: The cycle the reading fell in, if any.

snapshot.description: The observed `QuotaEntry`, as the channel reported it.

Output_QuotaProbeDto.description: An explicit diagnostic probe; responses are redacted and never stored.

Output_QuotaResetDto.description: The outcome of redeeming an upstream reset credit.

Output_QuotaSnapshotDto.description:
One live answer from the upstream, already persisted as cycles and blocks
by the time it is returned.

limitValue.description:
A decimal string, never a JSON number: a limit has to survive a
JavaScript `Number` unchanged.

metric.description: `requests`, `concurrency`, or any counter name the host charges.

userId.description: Exactly one subject, the same rule permissions follow.

Output_RealtimeAudioFormatsAudioPCMRate.description: A numeric literal validated through scalar conversion; object routing remains derived.

Output_ReasoningDetail.description:
Payload fields are optional because streaming detail fragments may carry
only a signature or identity. Encrypted data is never interpreted as text.

anyOf.description: Codex custom effort is serialized as an unsigned JSON integer.
Preserve backend-specific and future error codes verbatim.

reasoning.description: Alternative compatible-provider spelling. Kept separately on the wire.

reasoning_content.description: Plain-text reasoning returned by compatible providers (for example DeepSeek).

Output_ResponseMetadata.description:
Codex turn headers and opaque moderation/verification or buffering metadata.
These are stream notifications, distinct from user-supplied Response.metadata.

Output_ResponseOutputItem.description:
Native output items; input-only messages/references/triggers are excluded.
Same-shape items are reused; response-specific required fields use separate structs.

Output_ResponseStreamError.description: HTTP Responses uses flat errors; the Codex backend also emits nested errors.

Output_RewriteRuleDto.description:
One ordered replacement. Every write compiles the rule with core's own
compiler first, so a rule that would be skipped at assembly is refused
here instead of silently doing nothing.

paths.description: JSON array of dot paths; body target only.

ruleSetId.description: Ignored by `replace_rules`, which owns the set it is replacing.

name.description: The exact model name clients send in requests.

tier.description: Lower tiers are preferred; later tiers are the fallback.

upstreamModel.description: The upstream model this member sends, not a catalog reference.

weight.description: Positive relative weight within a tier.

Output_RoutingTargetDto.description: One exact operation/protocol key accepted by a conversion driver.

oneOf.description: Rewrites that hide one client application's identity from the upstream.

description.description:
A stable machine tag, `gproxy:preset:{id}:v1`, so a console can tell
which preset a rule set came from.

providerCount.description: Number of provider attachments, populated by list/get.

Output_SealedSecretDto.description:
A sealed secret as it travels: the envelope's own codec, and its bytes in
standard base64. Nothing here is plaintext, and nothing here can be opened
without the key the source sealed it with.

codec.description:
`plaintext`, `aes-gcm`, or `unknown` for an envelope this build does
not recognize. Carried so an importer can refuse early rather than
after decrypting nothing.

Output_ServerMessage.description: Generation and steering have distinct lifecycles on the same connection.

Output_ServerToolsCapability.description:
Server tool availability is separate from programmatic tool calling
(`ModelCapabilities::code_execution`).

Output_StatusDetail.description:
google.rpc.Status.details is a list of protobuf Any objects. Discovery
explicitly permits arbitrary payload properties; @type identifies their schema.

Output_StreamEvent.description:
Typed payloads for the HTTP Responses SSE stream. SSE framing and `[DONE]`
handling remain transport concerns; this enum only represents JSON data.

oneOf.description: Undocumented upstream heartbeat; converted to Claude ping or otherwise ignored.
Out-of-band response metadata emitted by the Codex Responses backend.

A future event type is ignored by converters. Known event payloads remain strict.
Native passthrough retains the original bytes rather than this marker.

Output_TlsPresetDto.description:
One client identity, ready to be stored as a connection profile's
`emulation`. The object is a `gproxy_client::EmulationConfig`, so a caller
copies it across unchanged rather than translating anything.

emulation.description: Only meaningful with the `wreq` backend; the others reject an emulation.

Output_TokenResponse.description: RFC 6749 §5.1. Both token values are plaintext and exist only here.

expires_in.description: The access token's remaining lifetime, in **seconds**.

refresh_token.description:
Rotated on every exchange: the one presented is consumed and this one
replaces it. Presenting a consumed refresh token revokes the whole
grant — see [`crate::operations::issuer`].

scope.description: The granted scopes, space-delimited, as they are recorded on the grant.

Output_TokenizerAuthDto.description:
Whether a source token is configured. The token itself is never reported
by a read; `reveal_auth` is the one deliberate disclosure.

totalBytes.description: From `Content-Length`, when the upstream sent one.

Output_UpdateProgress.description: Live byte counts and the current installation phase.

checked_at_ms.description: When this check completed, in milliseconds since the epoch.

current.description: The version this process is running.

latest.description: The version the manifest offers for this channel.

notes.description:
The notes themselves, when the host could fetch them. Never required:
a release with no readable notes is still a release.

notes_url.description: Where a human reads what changed. Straight from the manifest.

restart.description:
What the host will do to the process after an apply: `none`,
`supervisor` or `re-exec`.

rollback_available.description: Whether a previous executable is still on disk to go back to.

target.description:
The artifact key the manifest was searched for, e.g.
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.

Output_UpdateSchedule.description: What the scheduled check has found so far, and whether there is a schedule.

automatic.description:
Whether this instance installs what it finds without being asked.
**Off unless an operator turned it on**, and reported either way so a
console can say which.

interval_secs.description: Seconds between checks, or `None` when checking is switched off.

last_check.description:
The last completed check, or `None` when none has finished yet — a
process that started a minute ago, or one whose every check failed.

last_error.description:
Why the last check failed, when one did and none has since succeeded.
A console shows this rather than an empty panel that looks like "no
update available".

Output_UsageExchangeDto.description:
One upstream attempt inside a request: which provider and credential
served it, and what it cost on its own.

metrics.description: Dynamic dimensions and nested protocol-specific usage detail.

model.description: The upstream model name, which need not be the requested one.

quantities.description: Reported media/tool quantities, as exact decimal strings. Missing is unknown.

responseModel.description: The model the upstream response named, which may differ from `model`.

Output_UsageGroupDto.description: One bucket of a grouped aggregate.

key.description:
The grouping column's value. None is "the records carried none" — an
anonymous request has no user, a failed attempt no provider.

summary.description:
`truncated` and `scanned` describe the one scan every group came from,
not this group alone.

cost.description: The settled USD charge, read from its dedicated column.

exchanges.description: Detail of this physical call, retaining the existing exchange DTO shape.

metrics.description: Dynamic dimensions and nested protocol-specific detail; fixed fields are above.

model.description: The upstream model the call was routed to.

quantities.description: Reported media/tool quantities, as exact decimal strings. Missing is unknown.

requestId.description: Physical upstream call ID. A corresponding capture log need not exist.

responseModel.description: The model the upstream response named, which may differ from `model`.

Output_UsageRecordPage.description: One exact database page; provider and credential filters are SQL predicates.

Output_UsageSummaryDto.description: Totals over the records a scan covered.

averageOutputTps.description:
Output tokens per second of generation time, excluding first-token wait.
Only records with reported output tokens, TTFT and positive generation time contribute.

cacheCreationTokens.description: Total reported cache writes across all retention periods.

cost.description: A normalized decimal string, `"0"` when nothing was priced.

currency.description: USD when any record was priced; None when none was priced.

quantities.description: Totals of reported media/tool quantities; keys are billable metric names.

reasoningTokens.description: Part of `output_tokens`, listed rather than added.

requests.description: Number of physical upstream calls, independent of downstream association count.

truncated.description:
The scan stopped at its row cap. The numbers describe `scanned`
records, not every record the filters match.

Output_UsageTokensDto.description: Token counts exactly as the upstream reported them.

inputTokens.description: Ordinary input, excluding cache reads and cache writes.

reasoningTokens.description: A subset of `output_tokens`, never additive with it.

Output_UsageTrendPointDto.description: One fixed-width bucket of a trend. Present even when empty.

endMs.description:
Exclusive, always `start_ms + bucketMs`: the last bucket keeps the
width of the others even when the requested range ends inside it.

hasPassword.description:
Whether a console/portal password is set. `password_hash` itself has no
field here and no accessor anywhere.

oauthClientAllowlist.description:
None inherits the levels above; an empty list denies every client for
this user.

role.description:
Instance-wide role, `admin` or `user`. Organization and team roles are
memberships and are not this.

isDefault.description: Whether it is the instance default.

models.description: The catalog models that select it, by id.

action.description: The initial in-progress stream item precedes its search action.

info.description: Forwarding, management, portal and OAuth APIs generated from Rust types. Input and output schemas preserve their respective Serde contracts. Streaming events and WebSocket messages are documented alongside HTTP payloads.
